Andry · screens carrying an approval

The approved run171 plates, two reviews

Both source artifacts were read for screens tagged Approved in review, and only those screens were kept. The complete product, 171 screens contributed 66. The approved 171 contributed 105. Every plate below carries an approval; nothing untagged was brought across.

The two approved sets turn out to be exactly complementary — they do not share a single screen, and between them they cover the run end to end. What the older build approved, the newer one had marked carried over; what the newer one approved, the older one had not yet signed off. So the merged set is the whole product, 171 of 171, with each plate lifted from the artifact that approved it and its origin kept in the caption.

One discrepancy is worth recording. The approved 171 also carries small 171-build: chips reporting what the older build had said about a screen, and on 63 plates those chips read approved even though the older build never tagged them. This page follows the tags, which is what was asked for, so those reference chips have been dropped rather than left to contradict the provenance chip beside them. Design notes from the source captions — New, Reworked, audit references — are kept as they were.

#3 How it works

Wise — how it works — Four steps, then the house pattern the references never volunteer: capability, limit, risk, protection.

✓ Approved in reviewapproved-171W-12 copy

Trust & protection

Four things stand between you and a loss you did not agree to. Each one is checkable, and each one is written down here before you have given us anything.

1 · You own the animal, not Andry

When you buy units you become a legal co-owner of that specific animal, together with the other unit holders, in the proportion of units each of you holds. Andry keeps it for you as custodian. It is never Andry’s property and it never appears on Andry’s balance sheet.

If Andry failed tomorrow, the animals are not ours to be taken by anyone we owe. They stay yours and are sold or transferred for your account.
The same applies to a ranch. A host keeps your animal; it does not own it, and its creditors have no claim on it.
Insurance and maturity proceeds are paid to unit holders directly, by units held. Andry is not the payee.
2 · Your money sits apart from ours

Wallet balances and money held in escrow are kept in a segregated client account at a partner bank, separate from the account Andry runs its business from. It is reconciled against our own ledger every morning, and if the two ever disagree the system stops releasing money by itself until they agree again.

Held for you Segregated client accountNot operating funds. Not lent out.
Checked Every day, 06:00A mismatch blocks releases automatically
Escrow window 72 hours to confirm48 hours when you accept an offer. Unconfirmed means refunded in full.
3 · The animal is insured
Leadway Assurance · livestock mortality and theft POL-LW-2026-4471
Premium 1.25%, once, at purchase
Payout cap ₦1,200,000.00
Excess 5% of the admitted amount
Disease and theft are covered. Drought loss is not. Claims are paid to unit holders in proportion to units held.
4 · Where we stand with the regulator
We are not going to print a licence number we do not have Whether buying units in a live animal is a regulated investment product in Nigeria is being determined with our lawyers and the Securities and Exchange Commission. Until that is settled we will not claim a registration, an approval or an exemption. This page will carry the reference and the date the moment there is one.
Andry is a registered Nigerian company and follows the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation for everything it holds about you.
Your units are not a bank deposit and are not covered by the NDIC. An animal can die, and its value can fall.
You can take a complaint to the Nigerian courts or the SEC Nigeria complaints desk at any time. Using our own dispute process does not sign that away.
Everything on this page is in the terms you will be asked to agree to, in the same words. If the two ever differ, the terms are what binds us.

Livestock is a physical asset. You can lose money, and in the worst case you can lose the whole amount you paid. Read these three risks before you continue.

The animal can die

Disease, injury and theft happen on working ranches. Across our herd, roughly 2 animals in 100 were lost in the past 12 months. If an uninsured animal dies, your units in it are worth nothing.

The price can fall

Cattle prices move with feed costs, fuel, season and demand around festivals. A unit that costs ₦9,568.90 today can be worth less when you sell. Past price movement does not predict future price.

You may not be able to sell quickly

There is no guaranteed buyer. Selling depends on another owner making an offer, or on a pool filling. Some units have taken more than 60 days to sell. Do not buy with money you need soon.

What the insurance covers
Underwritten by Leadway Assurance, policy LW-AG-2211
Covered: death from named disease, accident, fire and theft, paid at the animal's last valued price minus a 10% excess.
Not covered: a fall in market price, slow weight gain, your inability to find a buyer, or loss during civil unrest and flooding.
Claims are assessed by the underwriter, not by Andry. Payment typically takes 30 to 45 days. Read the full policy
Andry is not a bank and units are not a savings product. Your money is not protected by the NDIC.
Tick the box above to continue. You can leave this screen without buying.

Account recovery is the door a thief walks through. The hold gives you three days to see the alert and stop it, and it costs an attacker the one thing they do not have, which is time.

Why lineage matters

Breeding value. A bull with three recorded generations and confirmed parentage sells above an unrecorded animal of the same weight. Buyers pay for the record, not the paper.
Disease predisposition. Known parentage lets a vet check for inherited conditions, and lets the ranch avoid mating close relatives. No trypanosomiasis susceptibility is recorded in this line.
One outcross. The paternal granddam is White Fulani, so this animal is not pure Sokoto Gudali. That is stated here because it changes what a pedigree buyer will pay.

When something goes wrong

#73 to #78 · 6 screens · 1 complete-171 · 5 approved-171
10:30
Offers

No offers received

When another owner bids on units you hold, the offer lands here. You get 48 hours to accept or decline before it expires.

How offers work

The buyer's money is already committed

When someone offers on your units, the amount is checked against their wallet at the moment they send it. An offer you can see is an offer they can pay.

You have 48 hours

Accept, decline or counter. If you do nothing the offer lapses on its own and the buyer's hold is released.

Nothing is charged to decline

Declining costs you nothing and is not recorded against you. The buyer is told the offer was declined, not why.

Accepting moves money, not units

The buyer's payment goes into escrow. The units move only once the host confirms the transfer against the tag.

What is in the file

Holdings

Every unit you hold or have held, the animal, the ranch, and the cost basis of each purchase.

Ledger

All 342 transactions since 06 Nov 2024 — purchases, sales, escrow movements, supervision charges, fees, deposits and withdrawals, each with its reference.

Proof of Life

The 418 records you have access to, all five parts, with the supervisor's identifier and the time each was filed. Photographs at full size.

Messages

6 conversations with owners, hosts and Andry, in full, with dates.

Verification status

That your NIN was verified, on what date, by which check, and every consent with its document version. Not the photograph of your ID — that is deleted 90 days after verification.

What is not, and why

Co-owners under 5%

They appear as Owner 14, not by name. That threshold protects them from you exactly as it protects you from them. You hold 26.5% of AND-4471-KX, so you are named to them.

Another owner's wallet or ledger

Not yours to have, even where you co-own the same animal.

A host's or supervisor's own records

Ayalar Ranch's books and Adekola Taiwo's licence file belong to them.

Exporting is not deleting

If you close your account, Nigerian anti-money-laundering rules require Andry to keep your transaction ledger for 7 years from your last transaction — until 2033 on today's date. Your messages, saved animals and profile are deleted within 30 days. Nobody at Andry can shorten the 7 years, and no export changes what is kept.

The records outlive the app. If Andry closed tomorrow, the custodian holds the ledger and you can still be paid what you are owed.

Filing standard
The owner cannot see the animal.
They see this.

A valid record, all five

1
Ear tag

Every digit legible. A blurred tag is the single most common rejection.

2
Side profile

The whole animal, standing, unobstructed.

3
Weight, kg

Read on the ranch crush scale, not estimated.

4
Condition note

Feeding, gait, coat, any injury. Plain sentences.

5
Within 24h

From the visit, not from when you get signal. The capture time is what counts.

Accepted, or rejected

Tag readable
Tag blurred

If it fails

Late

Filed after 24 hours. Counted against your on-time rate.

Still paid
Rejected

A part is missing or unreadable. Re-file and it still counts.

Unpaid until re-filed
Faked

Filed without standing next to the animal.

Licence removed

What you are never asked to do

Value an animal

You never estimate what it is worth. You record a weight; the market does the rest.

Discuss buying or selling

Not with owners, not with hosts. If an owner asks, say you cannot and the thread stays clean.

Treat a sick animal

You call the vet and record what you saw. Handling and medicine are the ranch's job, not yours.

This is what keeps your record worth something. A supervisor with an opinion on price is a supervisor whose weight nobody trusts.

Standard 3.1, in force 01 Jul 2026.

What gets assessed

Five sections

Have these ready and the visit is short.

Housing

Pens dry and roofed, floors sound, at least 3.5 m² per animal. He will measure a pen.

Feed and water

A current borehole water test, the feed store open, and weeks of stock countable on the floor.

Veterinary records

Vaccination and treatment logs for animals already on site. He samples and matches them to the animal.

Biosecurity

Quarantine pen usable today, wheel-wash charged, disinfectant log written up.

Record keeping

A movement book that reconciles: what came in, what left, who signed for it.

If a section fails

You get the findings in full, each with the remedy written out and a re-inspection date. Nothing is hidden from you and nothing is hidden from owners later. A first re-inspection is free. Fail the same section twice and the application closes for six months.

Once, at least 5 days ahead. After that the date is fixed.

Andry does not see the findings before they are filed and cannot amend them. Neither can you.

How fast

Three waves of 28 Recommended

Why the clock stops, and why that matters more than it sounds

A held escrow reverses automatically when its window elapses. If the clock kept running while a case was under investigation, the system would refund a buyer for an animal that may be standing perfectly well in a pen — or may be dead. Suspending stops the timer at the moment the host reports, and it resumes only when you release or reverse. Nothing here expires while you are looking at it.

The two ways out, and what each costs
Release₦50,347.50

Seller paid ₦49,000.00, fees recognised ₦1,347.50, units transfer to the buyer. Needs a valid scan first.

Reverse₦50,347.50

Buyer refunded the gross amount including every fee — no fee is revenue before release. Seller paid nothing, no units move.

The buyer may also cancel and take the full amount back at any time while this is open. Both parties are notified either way.

Release is disabled until a valid scan for AND-4471-KX is on file. That is a server rule, not a courtesy — a confirmation without a matching scan is refused whichever button you press.
